case.title: Handling a Rent Increase Notice in Finland
case.summary: A landlord cannot unilaterally raise your rent unless a specific rent increase clause was included in your original tenancy agreement. You should verify your lease terms and confirm if you received the required written notification at least two months in advance.

steps.title: Verify if you received advance notice of the increase
steps.detail: The landlord is generally required to notify you of a rent increase in writing. Depending on when your lease was signed, this notice must be provided well in advance of the effective date.

steps.title: Check your lease agreement for a rent increase clause
steps.detail: Review your original lease agreement to see if there is a defined clause that allows for unilateral rent increases and specifies the calculation basis. If no such clause exists, the landlord cannot increase the rent without your mutual agreement.

steps.title: Submit a written complaint to your landlord
steps.detail: If you believe the increase is unjustified or against the terms of your lease, submit a written complaint to your landlord. You can use the official Complaint Assistant tool for this purpose.

steps.title: Seek advice from Consumer Advisory Services
steps.detail: If the dispute cannot be resolved directly with the landlord, contact the Consumer Advisory Services for guidance. They provide general advice for private housing disputes.

steps.title: Request the basis for the increase
steps.detail: If your agreement has a rent increase clause, you may not always be entitled to an advance notice, but you can request the basis for the increase from your landlord for free.

steps.title: Update your Kela housing allowance application
steps.detail: If your rent is increasing and you currently receive housing allowance from Kela, you must report this change in your circumstances immediately through their online service or application form.

steps.title: Verify the required notice period
steps.detail: If the landlord notifies you of a rent increase, the higher rent can only take effect after this minimum notice period has passed, beginning from the start of a new payment period.
